title: What is a peninsula? Almost an island, still attached
description: A peninsula reaches into the water but keeps a land connection. Discover the detail that separates it from an island, from small headlands to whole regions.

cover.alt: An imagined green rocky peninsula remains connected to a larger coast by a broad grassy neck, with blue sea on both sides
cover.credit: AI-generated realistic illustration created for BrainiLab; an imagined coastline, not a named real location.

practice: Try another question about the world in the World Capitals Quiz.

sections.title: The piece that stays attached
sections.html:
A peninsula is land mostly surrounded by water but still joined to a larger land area. It reaches out into the water without becoming a separate island.

That remaining connection is the useful clue. A coastline can have plenty of bends, so look at how the land joins up rather than trying to count three perfectly straight sides.

sections.title: Not just an ocean shape
sections.html:
Cambridge Dictionary includes peninsulas extending into a sea or a lake. An ocean is not required for the name to fit.

Imagine drawing a pond with a long grassy tongue reaching into it. If that tongue remains attached to the surrounding land, you have the basic idea. The drawing needs no palm trees or tropical beach.

sections.title: Small point, big region
sections.html:
National Geographic describes peninsulas at very different scales, from small coastal projections to large regions. Spain and Portugal, for example, are on the Iberian Peninsula.

So a peninsula is a landform, not a size category. Its name tells you about the relationship between land and water, rather than how many people or countries it contains.

sections.title: Two ways to read a coast
sections.html:
A peninsula takes land out into water. For a different coastal shape, explore a fjord, where the sea fills a deep valley.

And when the land really is divided into separate islands, the group may be an archipelago. One map can hold several different kinds of coastline.
